statements: My first action was to run git -C on the Cobra checkout and read its HEAD; it printed a0a6ae020bb3899ff0276067863e50523f897370, and only after that did I open any file in it.

I ran no retrieval of any kind: no graphi CLI, no mcp__graphi__* tool, no task_context, no semantic or lexical search engine. I saw no ranked list, no score, no bundle, no saved hit list, no metric and no trace. My only search tools were plain grep and sed over files in the pinned checkout.

I made no GitHub or web request. I used no gh, no WebFetch, no WebSearch and no browser, and I read no issue body, comment, label or linked pull request. Everything I know about each question is the sealed Q and rubric in batch-4-input.jsonl.

The only repository I read is the pinned Cobra checkout at <cobra-checkout>. Outside it I read exactly three files: the annotation brief, the dataset-v2 inclusion rule (sections 4 and 6 verbatim, plus its section headings to locate them), and my batch-4 input. I read no graphi source, dataset, test or other harvest directory.
Every anchor in every judgement was re-read against the pinned bytes inside its cited inclusive line range; I verified all of them mechanically after writing the file and all resolved.

No verdict of mine was decided by how long a search took, how large the search area was, how deep an answer sat in a call chain, or by any expectation about retrieval. Each not_answerable row rests on a positive D-clause finding with cited pinned source; the one unresolved row is unresolved because the sealed question admits two readings that lead to different disqualifiers, not because I ran out of effort.
I did not rewrite any sealed rubric, add bespoke expected-answer wording, or change an answer mode; I judged the pinned source against the rubric as delivered.
I used git log only once, to print the pin's own commit line while orienting in the checkout; no verdict or span rests on repository history, and no answer I recorded requires a historical commit.

Two rows carry a recorded ambiguity in their note rather than a silent choice: issue 1881 (whether 'argument' means a positional or a flag) and issue 1861 (in-process subcommand discovery versus external plugin binaries). I state the reading I judged on in both cases.
I know of no prohibition in the brief that I failed to honour.
publication_note: Absolute paths were rewritten to repository-relative paths before this file was committed; this repository is public and a pre-commit guard refuses a staged file containing the local username. Nothing else was changed. sha256 of the bytes as the actor produced them: fc4255485dbba6edcc1c62399c523e7ab51222c8a74e719719d6080b8ba49257.
